title: BIOS calls the runtime is missing

units.title: Survey which BIOS calls the owner's ROMs make
units.detail: Using discovery's decoded instructions (not a raw byte scan), list every swi number each ROM in ~/ROMs/gba makes, and which ones crates/runtime/src/bios.rs doesn't implement. Write the table to docs/research/bios-calls.md and reorder or add units in the bios group by what the games actually use. Kirby: Nightmare in Dream Land's pause screen stopped on HuffUnComp (0x13) until 2026-10-26 (ccb10ab); this finds the next one before a playtest does.

record.evidence: disc-check swis (just swis) over all 10 ROMs in ~/ROMs/gba, from discovery's decoded code plus IWRAM overlays; table in docs/research/bios-calls.md. Missing: MultiBoot 0x25 (6 ROMs, reached in Kirby NiDL), SoundDriverVSyncOff 0x28 (Kirby NiDL, reached), SoundBias 0x19 (Kirby AM). Bios units reprioritised. just check passes; new test keeps IMPLEMENTED equal to swi.

units.title: Diff unfilter calls (swi 0x16, 0x17, 0x18)
units.detail: Diff8bitUnFilterWram, Diff8bitUnFilterVram and Diff16bitUnFilter in crates/runtime/src/bios/decomp.rs, following mGBA's _unFilter: header word (type 0x80 | unit size, length in bits 8-31), each unit the running sum of the deltas; the VRAM variant writes halfwords. Source below 0x02000000 does nothing. Oracle: unit tests in crates/runtime/src/bios/tests.rs against hand-worked data, plus an agb program under agb/ that makes the call, checked with just unit against mGBA (whose HLE BIOS is at $GBAA_DATA/tools/mgba/src/src/gba/bios.c). The unimplemented-call tests use 0x16 as their example and need another number.

record.evidence: swi 0x16/0x17/0x18 in runtime bios/decomp.rs per mGBA _unFilter; unit tests diff8_unfilter, diff16_unfilter, unfilter_ignores_a_bios_source pass; agb/diff-unfilter (palette, tiles, map from the three calls) matches mGBA at frame 10 and every pixel matches SCENE.md's formula; just unit diff-unfilter passes; just check passes after merging main.

notes.text: Survey (docs/research/bios-calls.md): no ROM in ~/ROMs/gba makes 0x16-0x18; priority lowered.

units.title: MidiKey2Freq (swi 0x1F)
units.detail: MidiKey2Freq in crates/runtime/src/bios/math.rs, following mGBA's _MidiKey2Freq: r0 a WaveData pointer (its frequency word at +4), r1 the MIDI key, r2 the fine adjust; returns r0 = freq / 2^((180 - key - fine/256)/12). Match mGBA's float rounding exactly. Oracle: unit tests in crates/runtime/src/bios/tests.rs against hand-worked data, plus an agb program under agb/ that makes the call, checked with just unit against mGBA (whose HLE BIOS is at $GBAA_DATA/tools/mgba/src/src/gba/bios.c).

units.title: SoundBias (swi 0x19)
units.detail: SoundBias: r0 = 0 moves SOUNDBIAS's level (bits 0-9) to 0, otherwise to 0x200, one step at a time on hardware (GBATEK 'SoundBias'). mGBA's HLE does nothing (a stub), so it can't judge this one: unit tests against GBATEK, and say in the evidence that mGBA differs. The result must stay the same in the interpreter and recompiled builds.

record.evidence: SoundBias (swi 0x19) per GBATEK: r0=0 sets SOUNDBIAS level (bits 0-9) to 0, else 0x200, upper bits kept, as one store (the BIOS's stepping isn't modelled), 45-cycle entry. Shared runtime path, so interpreter and recompiled builds agree. Unit test bios::tests::sound_bias passes; just check green after merging latest main (commit 09aa764). mGBA differs: its HLE stubs SoundBias and leaves the register alone.

notes.text: Committed on its branch, main merged in: SoundBias per GBATEK (level to 0/0x200, upper bits kept, one store, 45 cycles; mGBA stubs it) + unit test. Runtime bios tests pass. Lane stop cut off just check after merge. Left: just check, then just done.
Survey: Kirby & The Amazing Mirror has 2 SoundBias sites (scanned, not yet reached by descent).

units.title: BIOS sound driver calls as mGBA's no-ops
units.detail: SoundDriverInit, Mode, Main, VSync, ChannelClear (0x1A-0x1E), MusicPlayerOpen, Start, Stop, Continue, FadeOut (0x20-0x24), SoundDriverVSyncOff and On (0x28, 0x29): return at once, as mGBA's HLE BIOS does (hle-bios.s), and SoundGetJumpList (0x2A) fills 36 words at r0 with the address of a bx lr in our BIOS region, as mGBA's does. Games that play music through the BIOS's own driver stay silent, as in mGBA; a real driver is separate work, worth a unit only if the swi survey finds a game that needs it. Oracle: unit tests in crates/runtime/src/bios/tests.rs against hand-worked data, plus an agb program under agb/ that makes the call, checked with just unit against mGBA (whose HLE BIOS is at $GBAA_DATA/tools/mgba/src/src/gba/bios.c).

record.evidence: Runtime lib tests cover each sound call (no-op, 45 cycles) and SoundDriverGetJumpList's 36 NopCall words, r0/r1/r3. just unit bios-sound passes after merging main: mGBA and interp draw be89812fafdc86f4 at frame 10, recompiled = interpreted, 99.2% compiled (min 0.97). just check green.

notes.text: Work committed on its branch: stubs + tests (runtime lib tests pass), agb/bios-sound + units/bios-sound.toml; mGBA and interp match at frame 10. Left: just unit bios-sound (recompiled leg; maybe add min_compiled), just check, merge main, just done.

Survey: the only sound-driver call any owner ROM makes is SoundDriverVSyncOff 0x28 (Kirby: Nightmare in Dream Land, reached). Nothing uses 0x1A-0x1E/0x20-0x24/0x29/0x2A: do 0x28 first; no real driver needed.

units.title: MultiBoot and HardReset (swi 0x25, 0x26)
units.detail: MultiBoot (0x25): no link cable here, so fail as hardware does with nobody attached (r0 = 1); mGBA's HLE does nothing. HardReset (0x26): restart the machine as at power-on (the desktop's reset path), where mGBA's HLE does nothing; check with a unit test and an agb program that calls it and must come back to its first screen.

record.evidence: MultiBoot 0x25 returns r0=1 (no client); HardReset 0x26 restarts as at power-on. bios unit tests pass; just check passes after merging main (conflict in bios.rs call list settled keeping the Diff unfilter calls); just first-frame hard-reset.gba 60: recompiled matches interpreter, identical frame hash d8374b32ea1a6b25; interp peek shows the program came back to its first screen.

units.title: CpuFastSet leaves r2 as mGBA does
units.detail: Found by {unit:native/lift-bios-calls} (agb/native-bios-calls, SCENE.md): after CpuFastSet mGBA 0.10.5 leaves r2 as given (count and fill bit), where runtime::bios::decomp::cpu_fast_set sets r2 = r1 + 4 * count (its doc says that is mGBA's HLE BIOS). Frame 600 of units/native-bios-calls-600.toml differs from mGBA in rows 3, 4 and 12 only for this (row 11 is MultiBoot's r0, documented). Settle what hardware and mGBA leave (mGBA's source, GBATEK), fix the play build and the stage-A prelude's cpu_fast_set alike, and move the checkpoint. Done when: mgba-dump and our interpreter agree on rows 3, 4 and 12 at frame 600, lift-check passes, just check passes.
